title: TRACE: Discovering Task-Specific Parameter via Adaptation-Aware Probing for Continual Fine-Tuning

problem.claim: Continual adaptation of LLMs across tasks must preserve previously learned skills, but indiscriminate task mixing and sequential fine-tuning can dilute specialization or cause catastrophic forgetting.

gap.claim: Replay-based tuning and separate task-specific adapters can mitigate forgetting but add compute, storage, and management overhead.

contributions.claim: TRACE discovers task-specific core parameters through a short adaptation-aware warm-start probe and isolates the subset needed for each task.
The method identifies core parameters using importance scoring based on L2 norm and Fisher Information, and specificity analysis based on cosine similarity of parameter updates.
During continual fine-tuning, TRACE updates only the active task's core parameters while freezing the others.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present TRACE as a novel approach for discovering task-specific parameters via adaptation-aware probing for continual fine-tuning.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report superior performance across multiple standard benchmarks.
The authors report cross-model and scale transferability, including a small-to-large paradigm for guiding fine-tuning of large-scale models under resource constraints.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLMs are continually adapted across tasks while attempting to preserve previously learned skills.
Task mixing can dilute specialization, and sequential full-parameter or low-rank fine-tuning can cause catastrophic forgetting.
Replay and separate task-specific adapters mitigate forgetting but increase operational overhead.
TRACE uses adaptation-aware probing to discover and isolate task-specific core parameters.
The authors report benchmark performance and cross-model and scale transferability.

source_observation.claim: A short warm-start probe is used to identify a small subset of parameters essential for a task.

interpretation.claim: Brief task-specific adaptation traces may provide a basis for parameter-efficient continual adaptation.

application.claim: In resource-constrained continual fine-tuning, consider probing task-specific parameter importance before updating the full model.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when the identified core parameters fail to preserve prior knowledge or how much overhead the probing introduces.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide benchmark names, quantitative results, baselines, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not specify the warm-start duration, parameter-selection thresholds, or computational overhead.
The abstract does not report limitations or failure cases.
